{"CLEC9A":{"symbol":"CLEC9A","name":"C-type lectin domain containing 9A","summary":"CLEC9A is a group V C-type lectin-like receptor (CTLR) that functions as an activation receptor and is expressed on myeloid lineage cells (Huysamen et al., 2008 [PubMed 18408006]).[supplied by OMIM, Aug 2008]."},"WDFY4":{"symbol":"WDFY4","name":"WDFY family member 4","summary":"Predicted to be involved in autophagy. [provided by Alliance of Genome Resources, Apr 2022]"},"C1orf54":{"symbol":"C1orf54","name":"chromosome 1 open reading frame 54","summary":"Predicted to be located in extracellular region. [provided by Alliance of Genome Resources, Apr 2022]"},"CPVL":{"symbol":"CPVL","name":"carboxypeptidase vitellogenic like","summary":"The protein encoded by this gene is a carboxypeptidase and bears strong sequence similarity to serine carboxypeptidases. Carboxypeptidases are a large class of proteases that act to cleave a single amino acid from the carboxy termini of proteins or peptides. The exact function of this protein, however, has not been determined. [provided by RefSeq, Jan 2017]."}}

This gene signature is highly characteristic of conventional dendritic cells type 1 (cDC1): CLEC9A is a canonical, near-specific marker of cDC1s (cross-presenting DCs), WDFY4 is essential for CD8+ T cell cross-priming by cDC1s, and C1orf54 is a well-established cDC1 marker in blood atlases. The strong MHC class II signature (CD74, HLA-DPA1, HLA-DPB1, HLA-DRA, HLA-DQB1) plus CPVL and SNX3 further support a professional antigen-presenting dendritic cell identity, specifically the cDC1 subset.

